title: Character sprite animation with seamless transitions
author: arthan1011
selftext: A couple of month ago I've figured out a way to seamlessly animate character sprites. Here's [a short tech](https://arthan1011.github.io/c-demo.github.io/) demo. This whole process requires some planning, basic video-editing skills and two heavy video models that can be run locally. I usually write articles on tips and tricks with AI but this process is too complex - requires long video tutorial to cover everything and people don't seem to be very interested in overly technical stuff like this

replies.author: arthan1011
replies.body: All vidoe clips here are generated using Wan 2.2 - the main problem is to make transitions seamless. It basically imitates what's already possible with 3D animation and Live2D but with AI and much faster of course. I can't imagine how much time/money it would take to recreate this short demo manually.

replies.author: GigaTerra
replies.body: I noticed the character takes like an breath, is that part of it? Like basically you animate from Idle pose, to idle pose, repeating that first piece to smooth it out?

replies.author: arthan1011
replies.body: Yes, I create default idle clip first and the other ones "branch out" from it. But repeating happens because I haven't figured out better way to cut and merge clips - I've refined the process to make the switch happen quicker

replies.author: GigaTerra
replies.body: Yes, unfortunately with 2D animations transitions can't be calculated like vectors. It would be nice if there was an local AI that was purely created to do 2D transitions.

replies.author: GigaTerra
replies.body:
I am not OP but the difference here is that OP pre-rendered the sprites, where the games you mention render the sprites at Real-Time. OPs game can be small and will have no lag or network delay, but can only do the actions already generated (this is how most games work).

Also you are correct about somethings being easier to generate than others. It is all based on the data, chances are if you asked the AI to render an Real Time Stradegy game from scratch, it will do so poorly. You can however video record an RTS game, and as the AI to run a filter on it, so make it look anime or hand drawn for example.

replies.author: arthan1011
replies.body: There are only these short videoclips that can be chained together. To turn them into useful game asset one must make a transparency mask to remove background and make the "sprites" composable. Good thing there's a lot of "background removal" models out there to make keying automatically, MatAnyone2 for example
